name: 09b_queue_backend_down
why: The everyday failure: AnhurDB is unreachable (stack restarting, laptop offline). Nothing may be lost and nothing may be quarantined - the items simply wait. This scenario used to pin a declared divergence in `attempted`; on 2026-07-31 both sides adopted per-session blocking and it resolved, so the field moved into `expect`. The cost it existed to measure is now bounded on both arms: one attempt per DISTINCT SESSION, not one per item. That matters because the Go plugin runs inside a Claude Code hook with ANHUR_HTTP_TIMEOUT (15 s default) per attempt - a 50-item backlog against a dead backend used to be 50 timeouts in one hook, and Claude Code kills a slow hook, and a killed hook is a persist that did not happen.
on_failure: `pending_after` must list all three items in queue order: an item that disappeared while the backend was down is exactly the silent loss this queue exists to prevent. `quarantined_after` must be empty - an unreachable backend is not an attribution problem, and quarantining here would park recoverable turns where nothing retries them. `attempted` growing to one entry PER ITEM means per-session blocking was lost on that arm, and the hook is back to N x timeout; `attempted` shrinking to a single entry means the blocking went global again and one dead session now stalls every other conversation.
